summary: Tested the new password features end to end: the strength meter that blocks weak passwords (backend and UI), password events with WhatsApp-then-email alerts, the admin password history panel, the Forgot Password reset flow, and regression of the temp password and forced-change flow. Backend: 11 of 11 pytest tests pass. Frontend: all flows verified in the browser. No functional bugs found in the new features. One configuration issue: every WhatsApp send fails at Twilio with error 63007, so alerts always fall back to email.

minor.issue: Every send fails immediately with HTTP 400 Twilio error 63007: 'Twilio could not find a Channel with the specified From address'. TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM (a whatsapp:+14155… sender) is not a WhatsApp-enabled sender on this account, so WhatsApp never delivers and every alert goes by email. The fallback itself works (channel=email, whatsapp_attempted=true). Because the send fails right away, the 12s delayed status-check path ('failed'/'undelivered' after a successful send) was never exercised.

message_status() returns '' when the Twilio status fetch throws. '' is not 'failed' or 'undelivered', so the alert is marked channel=whatsapp, status='sent' and no email goes out. A status still 'queued' or 'accepted' after 12s also counts as delivered. Safer: treat an empty status as unknown and send the email fallback.

Neither applies _require_strong_password. RegisterReq and AcceptInviteReq only require min_length=6, so new accounts can still be created with weak passwords like 'abcdef'. This is inconsistent with the new policy on change and reset.
ResetReq.password has min_length=6, so a 6-7 character password returns 422 with a validation message instead of the friendly 400 'too weak' message. 8+ character weak passwords correctly return 400.

issues: As the history panel gains rows it pushes the Download / Archive / Delete buttons down (they align to the bottom of the header row). Cosmetic only.

action_items: Fix the Twilio WhatsApp sender: set TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM to a WhatsApp-enabled sender, or join the sandbox / approve the sender (error 63007). Until then all password alerts go by email.
In _send_password_alert, treat an empty or unknown status from message_status() as not delivered and send the email fallback.

Optional: apply _require_strong_password to /auth/register and /auth/accept-invite (and their UIs) so the policy is the same everywhere; raise ResetReq.password min_length to 8 or drop it so the 400 message is shown.
critical_code_review_comments: Scoring in server.py (_password_score) and lib/passwordStrength.js match exactly: 'password1' scores 1 (Weak), 'abcdefgh1' 2 (Fair), 'Abcdefg1' 3 (Good), 'NewPass12345' 4 (Strong).
Alert texts never include the password. The temp password is only in the admin API response.
The history endpoint projects only kind, actor_email, created_at and alert, with no _id, sorted newest first, limit 25.
A weak password on reset-password does not use up the token (the strength check runs before the token is marked used), so the user can retry. Reusing a token after a successful reset returns 400.
server.py is about 6400 lines and should be split into modules.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: the meter and disabled-state logic on /reset-password, /account#password (change-password-*) and the forced screen (force-password-*). The meter bars animate over 300ms, so wait about 600ms before checking colours in screenshots. Admin history panel: loads, empty state works, and it refreshes after the temp password dialog's Done button. Backend events and alerts: a client with no phone gets an email alert within about 1s. A client whose case has phone +15005550001 gets whatsapp_attempted=true and then an email within about 1s, because Twilio rejects the send right away with error 63007. Brute-force lockout, bcrypt $2b$, and httpOnly cookies plus CORS with credentials were spot-checked or covered in earlier iterations.
